title: Roads of Destiny: Compare the Two Final Knight Mates
summary: After the queen is taken, identify how a lone knight mates because pawns, enemy pieces and the distant king cover every escape.

nodes.question: The queen is gone. Can the knight finish the right-side pattern?
nodes.explanation: After Kxh5, Black’s own g5 knight and h4/h6 pawns occupy three flights. Nf4 checks by a knight jump and covers g6; White h3 covers g4.

nodes.question: How does the matching left-side pattern work?
nodes.explanation: After Kxb5, White’s king on a7 and pawns on a3/b3 are essential. They cover the squares that the checking knight cannot cover by itself.

branches.title: Right-side finish after Kxh5
commentary: Begin after Black has actually taken the queen on h5. Whether Black could refuse the earlier offer is outside this selected exercise.

Nf4# checks Kh5 and covers g6. Black’s Ng5 and h4/h6 pawns occupy three flights, while White h3 covers g4. A knight check cannot be blocked; none of Black’s pieces can capture the knight. This full fourteen-piece position is actual mate.
branches.explanation: Nf4# checks Kh5 and covers g6. Black’s Ng5 and h4/h6 pawns occupy three flights, while White h3 covers g4. A knight check cannot be blocked; none of Black’s pieces can capture the knight. This full fourteen-piece position is actual mate.

branches.title: Left-side finish after Kxb5
commentary: Begin in the separate source diagram after Kxb5. White’s knight starts on f5; this is not a continuation from the right-side position.

Nd4# checks Kb5 and covers c6. Ka7 covers a6/b6, a3 covers b4, and b3 covers a4/c4; Black’s a5 pawn and c5 knight occupy a5/c5. Every escape is accounted for and the knight cannot be captured or its check blocked: actual mate.
branches.explanation: Nd4# checks Kb5 and covers c6. Ka7 covers a6/b6, a3 covers b4, and b3 covers a4/c4; Black’s a5 pawn and c5 knight occupy a5/c5. Every escape is accounted for and the knight cannot be captured or its check blocked: actual mate.

exercises.prompt: Can we conclude Black had to take Qh5+?
exercises.answer: No. Kg7 and Kf5 are legal refusals in the earlier larger diagram. This exercise verifies the mate after Kxh5, not the entire queen-offer plan.

exercises.prompt: Why does the king on a7 matter?
exercises.answer: It covers a6 and b6. Along with the a3/b3 pawns and Black’s own blockers, that removes the flights left after Nd4 checks b5.

startContext: Final mating patterns only, after Black has accepted the queen on h5 or b5. Both complete fourteen-piece diagrams are visually reconstructed: native32 confirms Kxh5 at94 seconds; native51/52 confirm Kxb5 at143–146 seconds. The right pattern has White Ka7/Nd5/a3/b3/h3 against Kh5/Qe8/Nd7/Ng5/a5/c4/h4/h6/h7. The left has White Ka7/Nf5/a3/b3/h3 against Kb5/Qe8/Nc5/Nf7/Bf3/a5/h4/h6/h7. The branches teach Nf4# and Nd4# respectively, with exact finite certificates ending in actual mate. The queen offers themselves, refusals such as Kg7 or Kf5, the skewer conversion and the original seventeen-piece root remain outside this proof. These two mate-in-one exercises must not be read as certification that Black had to accept either queen offer.
